title: Certified Verification of Envy-Free Cake-Cutting for Five Agents
abstract: Filos-Ratsikas, Hollender, Latifian, and Tyrovolas (arXiv:2611.33149, Nov 2026) resolved the open polylogarithmic query-complexity problem for five-agent contiguous eps-envy-free cake cutting under monotone Lipschitz valuations in O(log^3(1/eps)) value queries and gave a Sperner-free existence proof via an anchor-cut, maximal-feasibility, leaving-agent Hall-robustness, softmax weight-balancing, and spanning-tree bisection architecture discovered with ChatGPT 6 Astra. We present a standalone zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization of 18 core combinatorial, Hall-margin, stability, Lipschitz, and bisection theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero Classical.choice) paired with an exact-Q four-mode certificate verifier (EF-CAKE5-CERT-1.0). Across 16 canonical certificates (0.246-0.934 ms, total 7.80 ms), all invariants replay identically over Q while rejecting 60/60 live adversarial forgery attacks.
ai_assistance_disclosure: Prepared by sole author Lluis Eriksson with AI coding, formalization, and drafting assistance from Google Antigravity; all Lean 4.35.0 proofs, exact-Q certificates, and adversarial tests were independently compiled and machine-verified locally.
